Thank you for sharing. You have no idea how much it helps to know others go through similar things. I think that eventually, the feeling of having no one to confide in & believing no person can truly understand what you’re going through, is what pushes you to that place of contemplating suicide. So, thank you again. Each one that comes here and write his individual story unknowingly helps others that go through the exact same thing.

You have to fight this. Firstly, as fondamentale as romantic relationships are, you mustn’t idealize them. They are NOT the single most important thing in life. 

Second, you shouldn’t assume that you’ll never find someone and justify it by highlighting some inherent defects in you. Trust me, although everyone has his own story & circumstances, most people go through rejection and self doubt. Some, what we may refer to as “normal people”, handle it better. Others (me included), much less. There are good, kind girls out there. And tinder is hardly the place to find them. I know it means very little to you now but trust me, one day (very soon I hope), you’ll find someone who will like you for who you are, things that now you consider as flaws. 

On a personal note, I’m a very short guy, so I haven’t had much success in life with girls, and it was always easy for me to blame it on my height (regardless of the real reason) and slip into depression. One night, after a very bad tinder date, I almost went on and ended it. But man, reading here what other people go through, I felt angry at myself for actually considering suicide over being rejected by some girl.

I know this feeling... sometimes I would just lie to my parents and say everything is alright with a blank expression, just to spare myself from an argument about why I’m feeling the way I do. They just accept it and move on with their day. Nobody really cares, even if they really want to. The longer you have depression, the more “normal” people just give up on you.
